facts.statement: Nakonanectes bradti was discovered in 2010 in Montana, United States.
facts.quote: Nakonanectes bradti is an elasmosaurid plesiosaur of the late Cretaceous found in 2010 the state of Montana in the United States.

facts.statement: The fossil was found by hunter David Bradt in November 2010 at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge.
facts.quote: In November 2010, hunter David Bradt stumbled on an elasmosaur fossil at the bottom of a narrow canyon on the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was partially destroyed by flooding before it could be fully recovered in 2011.
facts.quote: Before it could be salvaged in the spring of 2011, the shale nodule was partly destroyed by flooding.

facts.statement: The fossil was identified as a new short-necked elasmosaur species named Nakonanectes bradti.
facts.quote: The specimen proved to be a new, short-necked species of elasmosaur, subsequently named Nakonanectes bradti.

facts.statement: Nakonanectes bradti is distinguished from other elasmosaurids by having a relatively short neck.
facts.quote: Unlike other elasmosaurids, it has a relatively short neck.

facts.statement: The species possessed a neck with only 39 to 42 cervical vertebrae, which is much shorter than in most other elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: It also had a much shorter neck that most elasmosaurids, with only 39 to 42 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: The genus name Nakonanectes honors the Nakona people, also known as the Assiniboine.
facts.quote: The genus name "Nakonanectes" refers to the Nakona people, or Assiniboine.

facts.statement: The species name bradti honors the fossil hunter David Bradt.
facts.quote: The species name refers to David Bradt.

facts.statement: Found in the Bearpaw Formation, Nakonanectes lived during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian in the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in the Bearpaw Formation, a late Campanian/early Maastrichtian rock, making it one of the last known elasmosaurids to have lived in the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: Nakonanectes bradti is classified as an elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Nakonanectes bradti is an elasmosaurid plesiosaur of the late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Nakonanectes belongs to the parent group Elasmosaurinae.
The genus Nakonanectes is part of the family Elasmosauridae.
Nakonanectes is classified within the class Reptilia.
Nakonanectes lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers determined that Nakonanectes is a styxosaurine that exhibits convergent evolution with the South American Aristonectinae.
facts.quote: Danielle Serratos, Patrick Druckenmiller, and Roger Benson found that N. bradti, established by them to be a styxosaurine, is convergent in build to the Aristonectinae, short-necked elasmosaurids known from fossils collected in South America.

facts.statement: The presence of short-necked elasmosaurids in both North and South America suggests that this trait evolved independently in multiple locations.
facts.quote: This indicates that short-necked elasmosaurids evolved in multiple locations on the globe.

rejected.quote: N. bradti was only 5.1 to 5.6 m in length, making it one of the smallest elasmosaurids known.
